Chapter 5: To Jane, at Last

Dear Jane, I write this from the window seat at Pemberley, which I have claimed for my own and intend to defend against all comers.

You asked in your last whether I am happy, and I have been trying for three days to give you an answer worthy of the question. I find I cannot do it in fewer than eleven pages, and Mr. Darcy says the post will not bear it.

So I shall tell you only this: the library has a ladder on wheels, and I have ridden it from one end of the room to the other, and nobody has told me I am too old for it.

Come in the spring. Bring Mr. Bingley, and bring your good opinion of everyone, which I have missed more than I can say.

Your loving sister, Elizabeth.
